This is an application, seeking condonation of delay of 131 days in filing an appeal under Clause 12 of Letters Patent.
2. Despite numerous opportunities granted, respondent failed to file any response.
3. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent fairly submits that he may not be opposed to the condonation of delay, provided the main appeal is taken up for consideration.
4. In view of the aforesaid, the application is allowed and the delay of 131 days in filing the instant appeal is condoned.

1. The State of Jammu & Kashmir (now UT of Jammu & Kashmir) and four others are in appeal against an order and judgment dated 04.10.2023 passed by Learned Single Judge of this Court ["the Writ Court"] in OWP No. 811/2012 titled Sonia Devi vs. State of J & K and Ors., whereby Writ Court has awarded an amount of Rs. 4,16,000/- as compensation to the respondent along with simple interest @10% on the award amount except the loss of income.

sentences.text: 1 2. Impugned judgment is assailed by the appellant on the ground that the Writ Court has granted compensation to the respondent which is unreasonable and exorbitant and that the Writ Court has not taken note of the fact that there was no documentary evidence placed on record to support the claim of the medical expenses, etc.

3. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record, we are of the considered opinion that the judgment passed by the Writ Court is legally perfect and does not call for any interference by us in this appeal filed under Clause 12 of the Letters Patent.

The injury was suffered by the respondent due to sudden fall of a live HT voltage electric line and, therefore, the appellants cannot raise the issue that the disability was caused to the respondent by the aforesaid injury without there being any negligence on their part.
4. In the given facts and circumstance, the doctrine of "res ipsa loquitur" is clearly attracted.

So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Writ Court has followed the parameters which are applied for computing the compensation for the injuries caused in the motor accidents under the Motor Vehicles Act.
5. Learned counsel for the appellants could not point out any infirmity or error in applying the aforesaid parameters.
The respondent has admittedly suffered 40% permanent disability.

Thus,
viewed from any angle, the compensation of Rs. 4,16,000/- cannot be held to be unreasonable or exorbitant.
6. For the following reasons, we do not find any good ground in this appeal persuading us to interfere with the well considered judgment passed by the Writ Court.
For the foregoing reasons, we do not find merit in this appeal and the same is accordingly dismissed.

7. Appellants to deposit the awarded amount in the Registry, if not already deposited, without any further waste of time and the same shall be released in favour of the respondent after due verification.
(Puneet Gupta) (Sanjeev Kumar)
